method: python3 over scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json + node_modules/quran-validator/data/quran-verses.json (full-Quran scan for s-'-l ask-you verses, qul presence incl. fa-qul, 2:186 morphology segment-by-segment, verse texts for all refs); node scripts/cross_reference_tafsir.mjs on 2:186, 7:14-15, 26:23-28, 11:45-46; overlap spot-check via scripts/braintrust-v2/published-articles.md and community drafts.

results.notes: Substrate mostly verified: every listed yas'alunaka verse (2:189,215,217,219,220,222; 5:4; 7:187; 8:1; 17:85; 18:83; 20:105 as fa-qul; also 33:63) carries qul as answer-hinge, and 2:186 lacks it — morphology confirms the full 1S chain (sa'ala-KA 2MS object, 'ibad-I 1S 'My servants', 'ann-I 1S, fa-inn-I 1S, ujibu 1S IMPF). Tafsir grounding real: al-Muyassar inserts implied 'faqul lahum' (so the qul is FELT as dropped — minority gloss as candidate said); Ibn Kathir 'without any mediator'; Tabari/Jalalayn record the qarib-fanunajih sabab al-nuzul with God informing them directly. BUT the load-bearing universal 'exactly one question breaks it' is FALSE: full-corpus scan finds 79:42 'yas'alunaka 'ani-s-sa'ati ayyana mursaha' answered in 79:43-44 ('fima anta min dhikraha / ila rabbika muntahaha') with NO qul — near-verbatim to 7:187, same topic, one with qul and one without. Also the Zamakhshari/Kashshaf attribution is not verifiable from our four tafsir sources; verify Kashshaf directly or attribute generically ('a well-known balaghi observation').
results.corrected: Drop the false universal. Defensible core: among all 'they ask you' questions, 2:186 is the ONLY one whose subject is God Himself, and it is uniquely marked three ways — (1) the askers are renamed 'My servants' ('ibadi) instead of the flat 'they', (2) God answers in first person 'then I am near', (3) no qul relay in the majority reading (al-Muyassar's implied faqul is a minority gloss — flag the qul-drop as strong-but-not-unanimous). Handle 79:42 explicitly: the Hour question also drops qul, but its answer withholds the content ('in what position are you to mention it? To your Lord is its finality') rather than disclosing the Answerer — the two exceptions are the two questions whose answers cannot be handed over, one because the knowledge is kept, one because God refuses distance. Present the qul-pattern as a strong tendency with two structurally eloquent exceptions, and flag the two-exception mapping as a modern structural reading built on the classically attested 2:186 observation.

results.notes: Substrate exact against quran-verses.json: Iblis's request is verbatim 'ila yawmi yub'athun' in all three tellings (7:14, 15:36, 38:79); God's reply is bare 'innaka/fa-innaka min al-munzarin' in 7:15 and completed 'ila yawmi-l-waqti-l-ma'lum' in 15:37-38 and 38:80-81 — a different Arabic string from the petitioner's phrase. Tafsir grounding is explicit recovered tafsir: al-Tabari on 7:14-15 states verbatim that had Iblis been granted the respite he asked he would have gained immortality since there is no death after the ba'th, so God capped it at yawm al-waqt al-ma'lum; al-Jalalayn cross-references the fuller verse and glosses it yawm al-nafkha al-ula (the first blast); al-Muyassar 7:15 same (deferral to the first trumpet-blast when all creation dies). The deadline-swap is in the text and named by the mufassirun. Overlap non-duplicative: iblis-refusal-al-araf-7-11-15 covers the pride argument in 7:11-15, not the deadline swap — cite it as related. Drafting caution: frame 15:38/38:81 as COMPLETING the elliptical 7:15 reply (as Jalalayn does), not as a separate quieter utterance.

Substrate exact: 26:23 'wa ma rabbu-l-'alamin' uses interrogative ma; Musa's answers 26:24/26:26/26:28 are all genitives of lordship-over-X (heavens+earth, you+your forefathers, east+west), never a defining predicate. Tafsir grounding verified VERBATIM: al-Jalalayn on 26:23 glosses ma as 'ayy shay'un huwa' and states creatures have no path to knowledge of His haqiqa, knowing Him only by His attributes, 'so Musa answered him with some of them'; al-Jalalayn on 26:25 literally labels it 'jawabahu alladhi lam yutabiq al-su'al' — the answer that did not match the question. Recovered balagha, not imposed. One prose fix required: Pharaoh asks the ma-question ONCE (26:23); 26:25 ('do you not hear?') and 26:27 ('your messenger is mad') are mockery/escalation, not repeated demands for a definition. Correct framing: 'Pharaoh asked for a definition once and mocked twice; Musa answered three times, and never once with a definition.' Overlap: musa-firaun-dialogue-gaslighting covers the dialogue broadly but shows no ma/essence treatment — cite as related.

Substrate exact: 11:40 rescue clause names 'ahlaka' (with built-in carve-out 'illa man sabaqa 'alayhi al-qawl' — the promise itself had an exception clause; Tabari/Muyassar read the reply through it, and it strengthens the reveal); 11:45 'inna-bni min ahli wa inna wa'daka-l-haqq'; 11:46 reuses the same noun, negates it 'laysa min ahlik', and supplies 'innahu 'amalun ghayru salih'. Grounding solid: al-Jalalayn glosses 'laysa min ahlik' as 'an-najin aw min ahl dinik' (the saved / the people of your religion) — the exact faith-over-blood redefinition; al-Tabari opens the ikhtilaf explicitly and confirms the drowned son is meant. Two cautions for the writer: (1) on the mashhur reading al-Jalalayn takes 'innahu 'amalun ghayru salih' as referring to Nuh's REQUEST ('ay su'aluka iyyaya bi-najatihi') being the unrighteous act, with the variant qira'ah ''amila ghayra salih' making it the son — so rest the thesis on the well-grounded 'ahl' redefinition and treat ''amal as the new criterion' as a supported-but-contested supplement; (2) Tabari's ikhtilaf includes the minority view that the boy was not Nuh's lineage at all ('laysa min waladika'), which would dissolve the redefinition reading — mention it and present redefinition as the majority position. Central move is genuinely in the text.
